extracted.intended_audience: trans and gender-expansive journalists, newsroom leaders, journalism-supporting organizations, allies, and potential supporters/donors
extracted.subtask_short: about page for trans journalism org
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational 'About Our Work' page describing the Trans Journalists Association's mission, resources (style guide, workplace guide), membership, leadership, supporters, and reporting/communications priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate, nuanced coverage of trans rights and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trans Journalists Association 'promotes accurate, nuanced coverage of trans rights and communities in the media and fosters the careers of gender-expansive journalists.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the organization's central editorial standard and mission: news coverage should be both accurate and nuanced when reporting on trans people and trans rights. The page links this mission to resources (style guide, workplace guide) used to implement best practices in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and follow a style guide addressing common and complex questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The TJA 'maintain[s] a style guide that aims to address common and complex questions that arise when reporting on our communities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The style guide is cited as the resource for reporters to resolve terminology/usage questions and complex reporting decisions about trans people. (No stepwise rules are listed on this page; the style guide itself presumably contains the detailed criteria.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace guide with safety resources and newsroom policy best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The TJA 'produce[s] a workplace guide that includes safety resources, newsroom policy best practices, and other resources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames newsroom policy and staff-safety practices as evaluative criteria for newsrooms and employers: adopt safety resources and policy best practices to support trans and gender-expansive staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and career development for gender-expansive journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: The TJA 'fosters the careers of gender-expansive journalists' and 'has supported more than 1,000 trans and gender-expansive journalists through our workplace and coverage resources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs (peer mentorship, workshops, Peer Career Network) and membership services are positioned as methods to evaluate/support career development and retention of trans journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership inclusivity and dedicated community spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The TJA 'welcomes gender-expansive journalists of all self-descriptions and backgrounds, as well as allies interested in our work' and 'maintain[s] online communities for journalists, including dedicated spaces for trans, nonbinary, and gender-expansive to connect and discuss journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusivity of membership and provision of dedicated, moderated community spaces are presented as organizational standards for supporting community-building and professional exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and donor disclosure according to nonprofit best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The TJA's supporters are disclosed 'according to best practices recommended by the Institute for Nonprofit News.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates a standard that philanthropic partners and donor relationships should be disclosed publicly in line with recognized nonprofit transparency guidelines (e.g., INN recommendations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize safety, wellbeing, and digital safety guidance for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: The page references guidance such as 'How Trans Journalists Can Stay Safe and Well While Changing Their Bylines' and mentions digital safety tips (e.g., shared in webinars and training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety and wellbeing (including practical measures like changing bylines and digital safety training) are treated as essential practices and criteria for news organizations and individual journalists covering or working as trans people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centering marginalized perspectives and intersectional reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization's leadership and mission emphasize 'centering those in the margins, gray spaces, and at the intersections of life' and improving coverage and retention of trans journalists, especially reporters of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suggests an evaluative standard for reporting and newsroom practices that prioritizes intersectional perspectives and elevates marginalized voices in coverage and leadership.
